YouTube](http://img.shields.io/badge/youtube-nf--core-FF0000?labelColor=000000&logo=youtube)](https://www.youtube.com/c/nf-core) ## Introduction **nf-core/captnseq** [provisional name] is a bioinformatics pipeline for bacterial and plasmid TIS/Tn-seq (transposon insertion sequencing) data. It takes paired-end short reads from a transposon-insertion library, maps them to a reference genome, calls the insertion sites, and uses the per-gene insertion density to classify every gene as **essential**, **ambiguous** or **non-essential**. The pipeline is aimed at High-Throughput Transposon Mutagenesis (HTTM) experiments on large mutant collections. The current version covers the standard Tn-seq processing mode, from raw reads to gene essentiality. Genome-wide digenic interaction calling (synthetic-lethal and alleviating gene pairs) is the planned extension and is not part of the pipeline yet. You provide a samplesheet of paired-end FASTQ files, a reference genome FASTA and a gene annotation in BED format. Everything else runs with defaults that are tuned for Tn5-style transposon libraries, and each step can be adjusted with the [parameters](#key-parameters) below. ## Pipeline summary ![nf-core/captnseq metro map](docs/images/captnseq_metro_map.svg) 1. Raw read QC ([`FastQC`](https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastqc/)) 2. Adapter trimming of both mates ([`Cutadapt`](https://cutadapt.readthedocs.io/)), default adapter `ACTGTCTCTTATACACATCT` 3. Quality trimming and length filtering ([`fastp`](https://github.com/OpenGene/fastp)), with a sliding-window trim from the 3' end. Reads that fail, and orphaned mates, are kept in separate folders 4. Alignment to the reference genome ([`BWA-MEM`](https://github.com/lh3/bwa)); the BWA index is built from `--genome_fasta` 5. Mapping-quality filtering, name-sorting, `fixmate` and coordinate-sorting ([`samtools`](https://www.htslib.org/)). A sample with fewer than `--min_mapped_reads` mapped reads stops the run instead of producing silently poor results 6. Duplicate marking and removal ([`samtools markdup`](https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-markdup.html)), plus alignment statistics (`samtools flagstat`) 7. Insertion-site calling from the deduplicated reads ([`captnseq-toolkit sam2sites`](https://github.com/simonjeanneau/captnseq-toolkit)): one record per insertion site, written as BED and as normalised or raw, stranded or unstranded bedGraph tracks. 8. Assignment of insertion sites to genes ([`bedtools intersect`](https://bedtools.readthedocs.io/) and [`captnseq-toolkit sites2genes`](https://github.com/simonjeanneau/captnseq-toolkit)). The informative part of each gene can be restricted, so that insertions near the start or end of a gene can be ignored 9. Essentiality calling ([`captnseq-toolkit essentiality`](https://github.com/simonjeanneau/captnseq-toolkit), a Python port of the TRADIS essentiality script): genes are classified as essential, ambiguous or non-essential, with QC and changepoint plots for each sample 10. Compilation of the per-sample essentiality calls over all samples ([`captnseq-toolkit aggregate`](https://github.com/simonjeanneau/captnseq-toolkit)): gene x sample tables of insertion counts, read counts and essentiality calls 11. Run-level summaries: mapped reads, insertion-site counts and per-contig read counts for all samples 12. Aggregated QC report ([`MultiQC`](http://multiqc.info/)) ## Usage > [!NOTE] > If you are new to Nextflow and nf-core, please refer to [this page](https://nf-co.re/docs/get_started/environment_setup/overview) on how to set-up Nextflow. Make sure to [test your setup](https://nf-co.re/docs/get_started/run-your-first-pipeline) with `-profile test` before running the workflow on actual data. ### Input files **Samplesheet.** Create a comma-separated file with one row per sample (`samplesheet.csv`): ```csv sample,fastq_1,fastq_2 mutant_pool_1,pool1_R1.fastq.gz,pool1_R2.fastq.gz mutant_pool_2,pool2_R1.fastq.gz,pool2_R2.fastq.gz ``` | Column | Description | | --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `sample` | Sample name, without spaces. Used to name every output file of the sample. | | `fastq_1` | Path or URL of the gzipped R1 FASTQ file (`.fastq.gz` or `.fq.gz`). | | `fastq_2` | Path or URL of the gzipped R2 FASTQ file. | > [!IMPORTANT] > captnseq works with **paired-end reads only**. A row without `fastq_2` is rejected when the pipeline starts, as are FASTQ files smaller than `--min_fastq_size_bytes`. **Reference genome.** `--genome_fasta` is the FASTA file of the genome the library was built in. It can contain several contigs, for example a chromosome and plasmids, and reads are counted per contig. **Gene annotation.** `--genome_features` is a tab-separated, headerless BED6 file with one line per gene or feature to score: `chromosome`, `start`, `end`, `name`, `score`, `strand`. The chromosome names must match the contig names in the FASTA file. ``` chr1 37 1816 geneA 900 - chr1 2291 3482 geneB 900 + ``` ### Running the pipeline ```bash nextflow run nf-core/captnseq \ -profile docker \ --input samplesheet.csv \ --genome_fasta genome.fasta \ --genome_features genes.bed \ --outdir results ``` Replace `docker` with `singularity`, `apptainer`, `conda` or the profile of your institution. To try the pipeline on the small bundled dataset first, use `-profile test,docker --outdir results`. > [!WARNING] > Please provide pipeline parameters via the CLI or Nextflow `-params-file` option. Custom config files including those provided by the `-c` Nextflow option can be used to provide any configuration _**except for parameters**_; see [docs](https://nf-co.re/docs/running/run-pipelines#using-parameter-files). ### Key parameters | Parameter | Default | Description | | ------------------------ | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `--input` | | Samplesheet (required). | | `--outdir` | | Output directory (required). | | `--genome_fasta` | | Reference genome FASTA (required). | | `--genome_features` | | Gene annotation, BED6 (required). | | `--adapter_seq` | `ACTGTCTCTTATACACATCT` | Adapter trimmed by Cutadapt from both mates. | | `--trim_minlen` | `10` | Minimum read length kept after trimming. | | `--fastp_qual_threshold` | `10` | Mean quality for fastp's sliding-window trimming. | | `--mapQ_threshold` | `10` | Minimum mapping quality kept after alignment. | | `--min_fastq_size_bytes` | `10000` | Refuse to start if any input FASTQ is smaller than this. | | `--min_mapped_reads` | `1000` | A sample with fewer mapped reads fails the run. | | `--execution_mode` | `single_thread` | `single_thread` or `multi_thread`: selects the CPU, memory and time tier used by each process. | The complete list is in the [parameter documentation](https://nf-co.re/captnseq/parameters). For more details and further functionality, please refer to the [usage documentation](https://nf-co.re/captnseq/usage). ## Pipeline output The results directory contains one folder per stage. Every file name starts with the sample name. | Folder | Content | | ----------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `fastqc/` | FastQC reports of the raw reads. | | `01_cutadapt/` | Adapter-trimmed reads and Cutadapt logs. | | `02_QualTrim/` | Quality-trimmed reads, fastp reports (`QC/`), and reads that failed or lost their mate (`FAILED/`, `UNPAIRED/`). | | `reference/` | The BWA index built from `--genome_fasta`. | | `03_mapped/` | Filtered, sorted alignments and `flagstat` statistics. | | `04_filtered/` | Duplicate-marked and deduplicated BAM files, duplicate metrics, and per-contig read counts. | | `05_sitescall/` | Insertion sites as BED and bedGraph tracks, from the deduplicated reads. | | `06_intersection/` | Insertion sites overlapping each gene of the annotation. | | `07_statisticalreport/` | **Main results.** Insertions per gene (`*-genes_insertions.tsv`), the essentiality calls (`*.essen.csv`, `*.ambig.csv`, `*.nonessen.csv`, `*.all.csv`) and QC and changepoint plots (`*_QC_and_changepoint_plots.pdf`). | | `09_sample_summary/` | Run-level tables: `1_mapped_summary.tsv`, `2_insertion_summary.tsv`, `3_chr_count.tsv`, and the gene x sample tables `4_gene_insertion_counts.tsv`, `5_gene_read_counts.tsv`, `6_gene_essentiality.tsv`. | | `multiqc/` | The MultiQC report, `multiqc_report.html`, combining the FastQC, Cutadapt, fastp and flagstat results. | | `pipeline_info/` | Nextflow execution reports and the versions of all tools used. | In the essentiality tables, each row is a gene with its length, the number of insertion sites (`ins_count`), the number of reads (`read_count`) and the insertion index (`ins_index`, insertions per base). The classification uses the two thresholds reported in the same table, `F_threshold` and `N_threshold`. To see the results of an example test run with a full size dataset refer to the [results](https://nf-co.re/captnseq/results) tab on the nf-core website pipeline page. For more details about the output files and reports, please refer to the [output documentation](https://nf-co.re/captnseq/output). ## Credits nf-core/captnseq was originally written by Simon Jeanneau. We thank the following people for their extensive assistance in the development of this pipeline: ## Contributions and Support If you would like to contribute to this pipeline, please see the [contributing guidelines](docs/CONTRIBUTING.md). For further information or help, don't hesitate to get in touch on the [Slack `#captnseq` channel](https://nfcore.slack.com/channels/captnseq) (you can join with [this invite](https://nf-co.re/join/slack)). ## Citations An extensive list of references for the tools used by the pipeline can be found in the [`CITATIONS.md`](CITATIONS.md) file.
